text:
maria: quick checkin — I'm prototyping an "adaptive router" that maps incoming API requests to model variants and fallback chains. goal: prefer low-cost variant but fall back gracefully to higher-capacity/compatible variant when latency or errors spike. want feedback on policy shape and telemetry hooks.

alex: sounds good. are you planning the router to run in the gateway or as a control-plane service?

maria: gateway for hot path decisions (region, tier, feature flags). control-plane holds policy and rollout state. gateway caches policy for 1s to 10s.

jake: two quick concerns — quota attribution and request identity during fallback. if we reroute a request to a different model family, how do we charge tokens and show traces in the console?

maria: exactly — proposal: gateway adds X-Router-Decision header containing route metadata: "route=redwood-gpt-3.5;policy=adaptive-v1;fallback_count=1". telemetry pipeline consumes that and joins with token billing.

samir: what about REST -> gRPC transcoding? some frontends call /v1/generate (REST) while internal endpoints are gRPC with proto fields. fallback variants might have subtle proto differences. we can't silently drop unknown fields.

maria: agreed. gateway should preserve unknown JSON fields and forward as struct/Any when transcoding. if fallback model expects different proto, gateway must synthesize compatibility layer or reject with clear 4xx + reason.

rachel: from product POV we need clear rollout signals — latency p50/p95, error rate, and "semantic drift" (post-check evals). can the router emit canary labels per-request so console can slice metrics by rollout bucket?

maria: yes — the header will include canary_id when a request is routed under a rollout. console can then display per-canary metrics and a small evaluation sample.

ops-bot: deploy:router/adaptive-v1 started by tolga at 2024-07-17T15:10Z :rocket:

tolga: quick note — caching policy matters. when gateway caches a decision it can reduce calls to control plane but increases tail risk (stale policy during a canary flip). thinking TTL=3s for canary, 30s for standard rules.

alex: can we make the TTL adaptive? e.g., shorter during an active rollout window or when control-plane version changes.

maria: good idea. TTL calculated from (is_canary ? 3s : 30s) but bumped to 1s during first 10% rollout ramp. we'll add a header X-Route-Cache-TTL so traces show decision staleness.

jake: back to quotas — if request A goes to cheaper variant then falls back and retries on a more expensive GPU instance, who gets billed? we should bill by final execution but also capture attempted variant for accounting. otherwise usage graphs will be misleading.

maria: plan: billing records contain final_model, attempted_models (list) and token counts. console UI will show an "retry inflation" metric.

samir: telemetry ingestion needs to accept attempted_models as a repeated field. if we use protobufs, make attempted_models a repeated string in the UsageEvent proto. keep field numbers stable.

tolga: small proto snippet suggestion:
```proto
message UsageEvent {
  string request_id = 1;
  string customer_id = 2;
  string final_model = 10;
  repeated string attempted_models = 11;
  int64 input_tokens = 20;
  int64 output_tokens = 21;
}
```

maria: perfect. also add route_metadata as map<string,string> so we can surface things like "policy" and "canary_id" without adding fields every time.

alex: care about size blowup in telemetry — maps are fine but keep cardinality low. console should cap sample size for heavy attributes.

rachel: UX ask — in the rollout page show a "fallback rate" (percent of requests that hit any fallback) and "billing inflation" estimated $/1000 req change. helps decide whether to pause rollout.

maria: we'll emit fallback_rate and delta_cost signals. alerting rule suggestion: if fallback_rate > 5% and p95 latency increases > 20% for 5m, auto-pause canary.

jake: one more — how do we handle schema evolution on proto? if new fields are added to request proto, gateways that transcode must forward unknown fields. recommend using google.protobuf.Struct for flexible payloads or Any for typed plugins.

samir: +1. also add a small compatibility test in CI: gateway transcode fuzz -> server proto deser, ensure no runtime errors.

maria: next steps: I'll push a short RFC with decision points: where policy lives, header shape, billing fields, cache TTL heuristics, and canary auto-pause rules. please comment on that doc. planning a short sync Friday.

rachel: thanks — add a mock console screenshot for fallback metrics. helps PM/eng align.

tolga: adding a note — when fallback crosses region boundary we must preserve data residency headers and possibly reject. we'll include residency check in policy evaluation.

alex: great thread. minor nit: standardize header prefix X-RW- to avoid collisions (X-RW-Route, X-RW-Decision).

maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
